name: Alsobrooks HQ
subject: Here's your Team Alsobrooks Newsletter, Peter!
body:
Greetings #TeamAlsobrooks,

The past week on the campaign trail has been amazing. Thank you to
everyone who showed up and supported us as we traveled across the State.
Our ever growing people-powered movement is truly incredible.

In case you missed it, here’s what’s been happening for the past week on
the campaign trail and beyond:

We launched a new ad! We deserve someone who will fight for us. Angela
believes that we can go farther and ALSO do better for the people of
Maryland. Take a look at our latest ad linked below!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12981?t=1001&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

We had a great time visiting the University of Maryland Eastern Shore. It
was wonderful to meet with students and faculty to learn all about the
great things happening on campus. Thank you to Provost Dr. Allen and
Former Senator Jim Mathias for such an excellent tour. We can’t wait to
come back!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1018&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

What an extraordinary visit to the Perdue Henson Junior Achievement Center
in Salisbury, where they provide our young people with the knowledge and
the skills they need for academic and economic success. Thanks for the
tour!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1023&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

We had a wonderful meet and greet in Salisbury. I really enjoyed our
conversation about increasing accessibility to health care, transit, and
well-paying jobs. Thank you to Mayor Todd Nock, Council President D’Shawn
Doughty, Delegate Sheree Sample-Hughes, and Councilmember Michele Gregory
for gathering such an incredible group!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1024&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

Sunday morning, we worshiped at the historic Bethel AME Church in
Cambridge. Thank you to Pastor Randolph Fichett for inviting us to join
this service.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1025&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

We had the pleasure of stopping by the Play it Again Sam coffee shop in
Chestertown. While there, we got to chat with two young women – one of
which is the head of student government at Washington College – and spoke
about the importance of getting young people involved with politics.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1026&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

It was great to be in Chestertown to meet with the Democratic Club of Kent
County and the Kent County Democratic Central Committee, where we talked
about the importance of supporting hard working families. Thank you to
Minary’s Dream Alliance for hosting this fantastic event.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1027&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

I had a great time in Easton, talking about my work on climate resiliency
and how I’ll stand up for the environment in the Senate. Thank you to Mary
Tydings and Richard Marks for gathering a wonderful group.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1028&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

Thank you to the Talbot County Democratic Club for a great conversation
about how we can deliver for people across our great state. Thank you to
this incredibly energetic and uplifting crowd!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1029&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

It was great to be back in the Baltimore region for a meet and greet with
the Southwest Baltimore County Democratic Club. Thank you so much for
having us!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1030&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

We had a phenomenal time in Waldorf, chatting with folks from Charles
County about our plans for the U.S. Senate. Special thanks to Dr. Vinod
Shah, Ila Shah, and our friend Congressman Steny Hoyer for organizing such
an amazing evening.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1019&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

The energy in the room was on fire last Wednesday in Prince George’s
County. What a blast it was to see so many friends and familiar faces!
Thank you to Doyle Mitchell for bringing together such a warm group!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1020&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

It was great to join my friends Anne Arundel County Executive Steuart
Pittman and Annapolis Mayor Gavin Buckley for a wonderful gathering, where
we discussed how we’re going to go farther and do better for every single
Marylander. Thank you to everyone who came!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1021&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

UPCOMING EVENTS

Tuesday, March 5th (Baltimore) - Labor Luncheon - [ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12971?t=1002&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]RSVP Here
Friday, March 8th (Fort Washington) - PGC-NAACP Candidate Forum - [ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12972?t=1003&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]RSVP
Here
Saturday, March 9th (Rockville) - Montgomery Mass Meet and Greet -
[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12973?t=1004&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]RSVP Here

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/10004?t=1005&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]For more events, or to find volunteer opportunities in your area,
click here!

NEWS OF THE WEEK

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12974?t=1006&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]ABC News: Black women candidates eye historic Senate wins in 2024
“ABC News’ Rachel Scott sits down with Barbara Lee, Angela Alsobrooks, and
Lisa Blunt Rochester on ‘This Week.’”

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12975?t=1007&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Baltimore Banner: Political notes: Mayor debate next week; feeding
bills to the sharks; Baltimore and Senate endorsements
“We are fired up for Angela, and we can’t wait to get to work to make sure
she’s the Democratic nominee in May.”

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12976?t=1008&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]WTOP: Md. lieutenant governor visits Prince George’s Co. to push bill
aimed at tackling child poverty
“Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller joined County Executive Angela Alsobrooks to
encourage support of the ENOUGH Act of 2024, a bill aimed at creating
partnerships and funding solutions in communities where poverty levels are
high.”

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12977?t=1009&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Punchbowl: Alsobrooks Campaign Update
“Prince George’s County Executive Angela Alsobrooks’ second ad of her
Senate campaign touts her experience fighting for education, health care
and the new FBI headquarters.”

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12978?t=1010&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Kent County News: Senate candidate Angela Alsobrooks appeals to Kent
County voters
Democratic Candidate for U.S. Senate Angela Alsobrooks is confident her
experience as state’s attorney for two terms and as executive in Prince
George’s County will speak to savvy Maryland voters at the May 14
primaries.

GET INVOLVED

I know what you’re thinking... 🤔

Where did #TeamAlsbrooks get those cool shirts and how can I get one ???

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12169?t=1011&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ][IMG]

Well the good news is, our campaign store is now live! Grab some merch you
can wear to our next campaign event: [ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12169?t=1012&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Team Alsobrooks Campaign Store!

We’re extremely excited to announce that we’re accepting applications for
our Fellowship Program aimed at high school and college students. If you
know a young person looking to get some hands-on experience in politics,
encourage them to apply [ http://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/9723?t=1013&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]here!

Here on Team Alsobrooks, we’re proud to be a campaign powered by
grassroots donors. We believe in Angela's ability to go further and do
better for our communities, and we know you do too! It’s going to take all
of us working together to get Angela over the finish line this November.

[ https://alsobrooks.actionkit.com/signup/volunteer-form?t=1014&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Volunteer

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/12982?t=1022&amount=25&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Donate

SOCIALS

While we'll keep sending emails to keep you updated, the best way to keep
up with Angela is on our social media channels. Follow us on Twitter,
Facebook, and Instagram to follow along with us on the campaign trail!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/8814?t=1015&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Facebook

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/8815?t=1016&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Twitter

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/8816?t=1017&akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7 ]Instagram

Sincerely,

Team Alsobrooks

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=1159%2E52803%2EDBp0Q7

Dear Friend, We understand that we will not outperform corporate money with everyday people’s money. We can only out-organize them. How? **Look at this map.**
---
[ ](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzvO9dyZLmutArMaWDiwtWN5nWzDus5bua32DN2BbYqo0w&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=030424_tank_of_gas&n=2)
---
Since October, we have traveled 20,000 miles across the state, visiting with voters and every organization that would have us.
---
[ ](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzvO9dyZLmutArMaWDiwtWN5nWzDus5bua32DN2BbYqo0w&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=030424_tank_of_gas&n=3)
---
We are traveling across West Virginia to learn what every U.S. Senator who cares about the people needs to know. I’m doing what I have done for years: to understand the needs and advocate for them. I visit with people no matter their party preference. We all need food on our tables, jobs that pay a living wage, and infrastructure. The message I’m getting is that West Virginians want someone who will listen to them, put their needs first, and act to deliver. While other candidates attend “wine-cave” fundraisers, we are fueling my car to reach the most remote parts of West Virginia. [**Will you help us fund a tank of gas?**](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzvO9dyZLmutArMaWDiwtWN5nWzDus5bua32DN2BbYqo0w&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=030424_tank_of_gas&n=4)****

| | Let's Shape the Future of California Together
---
| Dear Peter,

As a fellow Californian, I understand the challenges and opportunities that lie before us. My name is Dr. Sarah Sun Liew, and [I am running for the U.S. Senate](http://enflyer.emsvc.net/lt_forward.php?s\[member_id\]=14742093;s\[member_key\]=D0ZNWsFELt;s\[lt_key\]=ec08f6b43b1b73b21b14efa04f9a2e2e) because I believe in a future where our state leads the nation in innovation, equality, and environmental stewardship.

My commitment to you includes:

**Economic Growth and Job Creation** : Promoting policies that support small businesses, encourage technological innovation, and create high-paying jobs for Californians.

**Healthcare for All** : Ensuring that every Californian has access to affordable and quality healthcare, because your health should never be a luxury.

**Climate Action** : Championing bold initiatives to combat climate change, protect our natural treasures, and transition to a sustainable, green economy.

**Education for the Future** : Investing in our schools and universities to prepare the next generation for the challenges and opportunities of the 21st century.

**Equality and Justice for All** : Fighting for the rights of every Californian, regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, or economic background.

**Comprehensive Immigration Reform** : Advocating for policies that provide a fair and humane approach to immigration.

**Addressing Homelessness** : Implementing comprehensive strategies to tackle the homelessness crisis head-on. This includes increasing access to affordable housing, providing supportive services for mental health and addiction.

Your support is crucial, not just for our campaign, but for the future of our state. Together, we can tackle the issues that matter most to Californians and build a brighter, more inclusive future for everyone.

**How You Can Help**

**Vote** : Your vote is powerful. Make sure you are registered and ready to vote on March 5, 2024.

**Spread the Word** : Talk to your friends, family, and neighbors about our campaign and what we stand for. Your voice can inspire others to join our cause and make informed decisions at the polls.

**Volunteer** : Whether you can help by canvassing, phone banking, or participating in digital campaigns, your efforts are vital to our success.

**Donate** : Every contribution, [no matter the size](http://enflyer.emsvc.net/lt_forward.php?s\[member_id\]=14742093;s\[member_key\]=D0ZNWsFELt;s\[lt_key\]=41bdc1f9cf419617b7c603e59ed89814), helps us spread our message and fight for California.

**Seek Endorsements** : If you are part of an organization, community group, or have connections that could lead to formal endorsements, we would be honored to have your support. Please contact us at [campaign@sarahforsenator.org](mailto:campaign@sarahforsenator.org) to discuss how we can work together.
---
**A Special Request for Your Support**

As we move forward, the strength of our campaign lies not only in our ideas but in the resources we have to share them. Today, I am reaching out to ask for your financial support. Your donation, whether it be [$5, $50, or $500](http://enflyer.emsvc.net/lt_forward.php?s\[member_id\]=14742093;s\[member_key\]=D0ZNWsFELt;s\[lt_key\]=d843bbbfaa0e0092a6273678c5de80b2), is an investment in our shared future, enabling us to amplify our message and engage with more Californians across the state.

Thank you for considering this request and for your continued support. Together, we can create a legacy of progress and prosperity for all Californians.

Warmest regards,

Dr. Sarah Sun Liew
Republican Candidate for U.S. Senate
424-343-7025
[SarahSenator.org](http://enflyer.emsvc.net/lt_forward.php?s\[member_id\]=14742093;s\[member_key\]=D0ZNWsFELt;s\[lt_key\]=53e03f0d86f7c812eefb390ccf5ccd30)

Abraham Lee

424-332-3779

| | _**Defining "Christian Nationalism"**_ By Sean Feucht
---
_The pen is mightier than the sword, and words are worth fighting for._
---
| | There is a fierce debate within Christian circles about the influence and scope of so-called "Christian Nationalism." Some want to apologize for it, others want to embrace it, but who really defines "Christian Nationalism?" This is critical. We are fighting a battle not about ideology, but about the very language we use every single day. Truth doesn't change, but words certainly do.

A recent report from the Public Religion Research Institute claims that 55% of Republicans "qualify" as Christian nationalists. Did you catch that word? Qualify. We "qualify" as Christian Nationalists because they are creating the definition. I refuse to cede defining "Christian Nationalism" to those who weaponize and politicize the dictionary. If you can't properly define what a woman is, you lose the right to define "Christian Nationalist."

Let's unpack the term "Christian Nationalism." Separate it into its parts and something becomes clear; the people who define "Christian Nationalism" hate both. Christianity and Nationalism are anathema to the liberal ideology. The globalist mindset we see of our leaders pushing today was flatly rejected by God in Genesis. In Genesis 11, there was only one people and one tongue, and yet the Lord, "scattered them over the face of the whole earth." That's how globalism should be dealt with. body:
This is why I’m running for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.
#
Peter — I’m running for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat because I want to take back power for everyday people. **Here’s what that means to me:**
**Holding politicians accountable:** Too many of our leaders have been bought off by the massive corporations responsible for stripping our communities for parts. That’s why I’m fighting to abolish corporate PACs and ban insider trading for members of Congress — and it’s why I’m holding myself and my campaign to that same standard.
**Putting people in charge of their own lives:** Politicians like Josh Hawley are obsessed with controlling every aspect of our lives. I’m committed to restoring abortion access and protecting reproductive freedom in all 50 states by ending the filibuster and codifying Roe v. Wade — finally giving people the power to make decisions about their own bodies, families, and economic opportunities.
**Showing up for working Missourians:** Real workers are tired of corporate elites and frauds writing the rules we all have to live by. I’ll always stand on the side of working people by continuing to fight for the right to organize and pushing back against anti-union “Right-to-Work” scams in Missouri + all across the country.
**A Marshall Plan for the Midwest:** DC politicians spent decades wasting trillions of dollars on corporate handouts and forever wars. Now, it’s time to invest in the workers and communities that make our country strong so we can rebuild our forgotten towns and finally start making stuff in America again.

| | The Backstory: We are closely monitoring the unfolding of [Project 2025](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=uvcmBqlSboJEG9mlbJ7kX1yvxOtPzg2wm6Vo-jyxYzI.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucHJvamVjdDIwMjUub3JnLyIsInIiOiJjZGFkMzE3ZS00NGZlLTQ1OTEtOTFhOC0zOWNjM2E3OTcxZDEiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiIyNzdlN2Y0YS0wMGUzLTQ4ZmMtYmI5Ny02NTRiM2ZhMzc0YTgifQ) in Yakima. If you're unfamiliar, it's a plan aimed at reshaping the US Government should Donald Trump be reelected. The strategy, in essence, involves firing government workers and replacing them with Trump loyalists, intending to transform government agencies into tools of the President.In Yakima, our newly elected city council comprises five MAGA patriots, whose election methods are questionable. It seems they may have utilized their church, where they all attend, to run their political campaign. Additionally, one council member doesn't even reside in Yakima.Their initial action was to immediately fire the city manager by 'Suspending the Rules.' Now, they are poised to diminish the significance of committees like the Historic Preservation Committee, Bike and Pedestrian Committee, and the Yakima Tree Board by making them subcommittees of the planning board. Furthermore, they plan to remove the Community Integration Committee (diversity focus) and the Sustainable Yakima Committee from the city code. This move stifles community input in the decision-making process. It's [Project 25](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=uvcmBqlSboJEG9mlbJ7kX1yvxOtPzg2wm6Vo-jyxYzI.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucHJvamVjdDIwMjUub3JnLyIsInIiOiJjZGFkMzE3ZS00NGZlLTQ1OTEtOTFhOC0zOWNjM2E3OTcxZDEiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiIyNzdlN2Y0YS0wMGUzLTQ4ZmMtYmI5Ny02NTRiM2ZhMzc0YTgifQ) in action. For more information: Contact Coleen Anderson at [coleenanderson22@gmail.com](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=smAKhkzoXct1UnXESTQeS4xTwVA9w0TzdYjhsEeXP9E.eyJ1IjoibWFpbHRvOmNvbGVlbmFuZGVyc29uMjJAZ21haWwuY29tIiwiciI6ImNkYWQzMTdlLTQ0ZmUtNDU5MS05MWE4LTM5Y2MzYTc5NzFkMSIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjI3N2U3ZjRhLTAwZTMtNDhmYy1iYjk3LTY1NGIzZmEzNzRhOCJ9)

| | 3\. Turning the Tide: Inspiring Voter Engagement in Upcoming Elections
---
| | The biggest threat to the upcoming election is lack of interest in the election. John Halpin, writing for [The Liberal Patriot](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=MbyLZlp_knRglq8opBKUx1LL08ln9EdMCNcfZJFk3PQ.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubGliZXJhbHBhdHJpb3QuY29tL3AvYW1lcmljYW5zLWFyZW50LXBheWluZy1jbG9zZS1hdHRlbnRpb24iLCJyIjoiMGRkZjZjN2EtMTIwOC00MWVlLTE1MDMtNmM4ZTM4ZGYyMTI5IiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiMjc3ZTdmNGEtMDBlMy00OGZjLWJiOTctNjU0YjNmYTM3NGE4In0), speaks to an Economist/YouGov poll showing that the majority of potential voters could not care less about the election.
---
| [](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=NaYNMxSZOgSTvbfuTOts9RY_gsWyK_cc9S16wd0Iu5A.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubGliZXJhbHBhdHJpb3QuY29tL3AvYW1lcmljYW5zLWFyZW50LXBheWluZy1jbG9zZS1hdHRlbnRpb24iLCJyIjoiZDNjOTcyZWUtZWIwZS00YjY4LWU0YTYtZDZmMTIxMmMwNjFhIiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiMjc3ZTdmNGEtMDBlMy00OGZjLWJiOTctNjU0YjNmYTM3NGE4In0)
---
| | But where do we find hope in re-engaging people in the political process? Firstly, we're in a better position than we think. According to the [Washington Secretary of State](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=K9QoImjlZlu0TKCFHYd2flU3BuWEtpehfoktJtsdls8.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc29zLndhLmdvdi8iLCJyIjoiMTVkN2VkNzYtZWI3Yi00ZmY2LTgzMzctNDkxYmE3MGEzNDRlIiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiMjc3ZTdmNGEtMDBlMy00OGZjLWJiOTctNjU0YjNmYTM3NGE4In0) the average voter turnout in Central Washington is pretty close to the national average of 66%, and considering that only 37% of eligible voters participated in all of the last three Presidential Elections, we're doing relatively well ([Pew Research, July 2022](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=iWtdrCo6oqASI3GHI5Fd5wAvvrRGqI3uYrQC8duMs9s.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucGV3cmVzZWFyY2gub3JnL3BvbGl0aWNzLzIwMjMvMDcvMTIvdm90ZXItdHVybm91dC0yMDE4LTIwMjIvIiwiciI6IjE1ZDdlZDc2LWViN2ItNGZmNi04MzM3LTQ5MWJhNzBhMzQ0ZSIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjI3N2U3ZjRhLTAwZTMtNDhmYy1iYjk3LTY1NGIzZmEzNzRhOCJ9)). Why do we look good? Because we have four of the five lowest-scoring subgroups on that poll: Income under $50,000, Hispanic, Age 18-29, and Independent. There is literally nowhere to go but up.Additionally, the top concerns of Americans - Inflation, Healthcare, Immigration, and Jobs - are also our concerns ([Economist/YouGov poll](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=kCQY9BeLUB46x-ngVd5Ojk6Uk-xt8wnaHdLefu-pspg.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly90b2RheS55b3Vnb3YuY29tL3RvcGljcy9wb2xpdGljcy9leHBsb3JlL3RvcGljL1RoZV9FY29ub21pc3RfWW91R292X3BvbGxzIiwiciI6IjE1ZDdlZDc2LWViN2ItNGZmNi04MzM3LTQ5MWJhNzBhMzQ0ZSIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjI3N2U3ZjRhLTAwZTMtNDhmYy1iYjk3LTY1NGIzZmEzNzRhOCJ9), select poll 6. Most Important Issues). So, we have two significant advantages: we're starting from an average position, and we have a large portion of our population that still does not vote but can. Furthermore, we share the concerns of many others, which means we have the support of others who will be working on this issue. There's further encouragement from an unlikely source. The Republican Party in Central Washington is making strides in getting voter turnout among the younger population, which is encouraging. In fact, if voter turnout in the recent primary is any indication, the Republican Party dominates our youth in Central Washington.Rural Americans United emphasizes that over 80% of the people living in Central Washington have not heard a pro-democratic message. And for those under 25, it's closer to 100%!
---
| |
---
| There's no better proof than seeing [17-year-olds who voted in the primary](https://www.ruralamericansunited.org/so/03Ou7QlpI/c?w=gSoEI60CREEaiRqPrAMugMPGdmokJvjboZHQ1IkixBw.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc29zLndhLmdvdi9lbGVjdGlvbnMvZGF0YS1yZXNlYXJjaC9lbGVjdGlvbi1kYXRhLWFuZC1tYXBzL2JhbGxvdC1yZXR1cm4tc3RhdGlzdGljcyIsInIiOiJhOTcxNjMwMC00ZWMzLTRiOWMtOGI5MS0wMzc2MzNjMzVkMzgiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiIyNzdlN2Y0YS0wMGUzLTQ4ZmMtYmI5Ny02NTRiM2ZhMzc0YTgifQ) almost exclusively supporting the Republican Party. That's why we broadcast pro-democratic messages - to educate, remind, and persuade people that democratic values are their values. Otherwise, all they hear is Republican Party rhetoric. And our young adults deserve better.

| | | My fellow Americans - this is Speaker Mike Johnson.

_You've never seen fire and brimstone until you've gone head-to-head with Trump-hating socialists. _

So you can imagine the immediate wrath I faced when I went on record supporting Donald J. Trump for President. I was just talking to my friend, Steve Scalise - he faced the same thing when he endorsed Trump too.

_**[He and I agree: as strong Pro-Trump Conservatives, we've got to stick together.](http://links.thegopreport.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=cdbf65d0a7b14572a4ac76067cb0f7c4&_e=uun9DH-_y6rsSn9zZO1mIJN1eUT14u_MEo23utzsiHuBh85qfYiYimQYVJs8rL5hsvvWFDIG-qWsuKzx06L5BRmI5_xJ7QELWkVOyttX5t8vEJP6fI54xf_ETzwkymG1hyLJpVsV1voITDSY6bq-kcHuHWryjFZ2lqtsPErFd1nUwJCspLRoq6XQEviKnqWzf_MvilHYvhOUg3dvB4lnyvm_5srPJgbKsH1Ce84NqbHeUhh5eLUR1TG1Nwz5jHq8kIE2ZxPl8RA3IVX5Jl9XaIt4gtHnXt9JbSA0H-pizVkqjvYDZX5K4NlFKfX_txKW6sUUaxliKWWP5HiXKVpQpd3Pe4t8XBWkoRDI38HVjfAKikQPi1Ih4BBjrIz0rxAEvPDDrFrANesUAOhmJfww2K7xJqrbWHmH7n9f8HnNmaU%3D "He and I agree: as strong Pro-Trump Conservatives, we’ve got to stick together.")**_

That's because the anti-Trump Media... Young radicals on college campuses... the holier-than-thou elites in Hollywood... Democrat Super PACs... Joe Biden's army of megadonors... They are fully committed to destroying our movement and replacing EVERY LAST ONE OF US with a Liberal Democrat.

But wait, that's not even the half of it. It gets worse:
** Problem #1: ** We have TWO imminent Special Elections and Democrats committed more than five million dollars to install more Liberals.

** Problem #2: ** House Democrats have forty million bucks stashed away to attack pro-Trump Conservatives like us.

** Problem #3: ** Joe Biden just bragged about raising a million bucks in a SINGLE DAY attacking President Trump.
I cannot stress the urgency of the situation enough. Early voting is about to start in the first Special Election AND the Left's fundraising advantage grows by the minute...

_**[So as one of my first moves of the election year, I'm teaming up with my fellow Louisianian, Steve Scalise, to set a goal of raising one million dollars between now and the end of the month.](http://links.thegopreport.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=cdbf65d0a7b14572a4ac76067cb0f7c4&_e=uun9DH-_y6rsSn9zZO1mIJN1eUT14u_MEo23utzsiHuBh85qfYiYimQYVJs8rL5hsvvWFDIG-qWsuKzx06L5BRmI5_xJ7QELWkVOyttX5t8vEJP6fI54xf_ETzwkymG1hyLJpVsV1voITDSY6bq-kcHuHWryjFZ2lqtsPErFd1nUwJCspLRoq6XQEviKnqWzf_MvilHYvhOUg3dvB4lnyvm_5srPJgbKsH1Ce84NqbHeUhh5eLUR1TG1Nwz5jHq8kIE2ZxPl8RA3IVX5Jl9XaHvPFSJSAbzfdG_qPn8Pp0dfRvnZNx05pJZT-asCbB6YohkJ-kF3abZfFGnuYgPaB_q0hTUgetNsRusvYx2mai0b57RjGCkqyzfY67RHkX6A5mPza3uX5O_svEOdxs4ZqHtWlqg4eq9FjZhUISGzz3U%3D "So as one of my first moves of the election year, I’m teaming up with my fellow Louisianian, Steve Scalise, to set a goal of raising one million dollars between now and the end of the month.")**_

I know, I know - that's a big goal. I get that. But that's as low as I could possibly make it to fully fund our campaign operations in every must-win swing state.

If we fail to hit it, the consequences would be unthinkable. We'd have no choice but to: **1) ** SCRAP our get-out-the-vote operations, **2) ** SLASH the budget for our ad campaigns, and **3) ** Throw our digital outreach plans IN THE TRASH CAN.

Nothing - and I mean NOTHING - would be worse for our plans to defend our razor-thin House Majority. **That 's why I'm calling for reinforcements. **

_I know the economy is in bad shape under Joe Biden. So if that 's preventing you from pitching in $100 or $50 - I completely understand. But if you can afford JUST $10 or even $5, I would be grateful beyond measure. _

_**[I only ask everyone reading this to pitch for a few bucks or whatever you can afford.](http://links.thegopreport.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=cdbf65d0a7b14572a4ac76067cb0f7c4&_e=uun9DH-_y6rsSn9zZO1mIJN1eUT14u_MEo23utzsiHuBh85qfYiYimQYVJs8rL5hsvvWFDIG-qWsuKzx06L5BRmI5_xJ7QELWkVOyttX5t8vEJP6fI54xf_ETzwkymG1hyLJpVsV1voITDSY6bq-kcHuHWryjFZ2lqtsPErFd1nUwJCspLRoq6XQEviKnqWzf_MvilHYvhOUg3dvB4lnyvm_5srPJgbKsH1Ce84NqbHeUhh5eLUR1TG1Nwz5jHq8kIE2ZxPl8RA3IVX5Jl9XaMvM8mw4AqQ7dpOPCjRELSBfN_VrWrXKoJ53BH66qU_CeszmYeFK1zM1RIin5e1R6Fcz3q2ihui-eYy02bN82eVePB7E7UQ8CS4DE8gncC5eCvDt1DeiPSFrj-V9OIgpdBxo0tMyHEwkxSG3TzCmESQ%3D "I only ask everyone reading this to pitch for a few bucks or whatever you can afford.")**_

When the stakes are this high, that's what will be the difference between saving our Republican Majority and losing to the Trump-hating Democrats. So can I count on you to pitch in SOMETHING?

This decision in Alabama has already had devastating consequences for women in the state who were undergoing IVF since most clinics and hospitals have now paused IVF altogether.

IVF is widely used by individuals across the country to conceive for a range of reasons, including veterans who have suffered injuries, couples who suffer from infertility, individuals who have undergone chemotherapy, and more.

That starts with protecting vulnerable seats like mine in PA-07. | = | Last week, I joined MSNBC to discuss the Alabama Supreme Court ruling that has virtually ended in vitro fertilization in the state and to discuss my bill to safeguard IVF: = | = Since the Dobbs decision, I knew that Republicans’ position that life begins at conception would mean further restrictions beyond abortion bans, which is why I started working on this bill almost immediately to protect IVF. This decision in Alabama has already had devastating consequences for women in the state who were undergoing IVF since most clinics and hospitals have now paused IVF altogether. But this is no different than an abortion ban. It’s not based on science or medical reasoning – it’s all about the government’s ability to control what women do with their bodies. name: Chrissy
subject: What I've been up to
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chrissy Houlahan for Congress
body:
A Note From Chrissy
As I write this, we’re about to vote - once again - to prevent a partial government shutdown and give negotiators more time to work out the details of a longer-term spending deal. Sigh. No comment.

From my 83rd town hall to a visit to the southern border, 2024 is off to a busy start. I'm so excited to share the details with you in this month's newsletter!

A Town Hall for the Whole Family

Among a lot of other hats I've worn, I'm a very proud mother of wonderful daughters. Since I joined Congress, I've made it a top priority to extend a helping hand to the children and families in our community. That's why I've championed expanded paid family leave, better care for mothers, infant nutrition, and student skills training to ensure their success in our economy. In Kennett Square, at my 83rd town hall, I invited neighbors to hear about the work I've been doing for families, give me feedback and advice about what else I can do, learn about important federal resources, and ask questions about the next steps in our fight for parents and families in Chester and Berks counties. I'm so grateful to all of the attendees who came to participate in this productive conversation!

The Fight for Bipartisan Border Security and Immigration Reform

On my recent visit to the southern border in El Paso, one thing was clear: Our immigration system is broken.

The American people deserve real solutions to this complex issue right now, and that can only happen through compromise and collaboration across both sides of the aisle. These practical solutions already exist, like Rep. Escobar's bipartisan Dignity Act, which would provide more money for border enforcement and infrastructure, require that employees verify their immigration status, provide a path to citizenship for "Dreamers," and establish a path to permanent residency status for eligible people without lawful immigration status. We have the tools to address this issue NOW – including the bipartisan compromise negotiated in the Senate - and it’s shameful that Republicans tanked the first real legislative progress on this issue in years because Donald Trump asked them to.

Do you need assistance with a federal agency?

My office was recently contacted by a woman named Soumya in Malvern. She told us that she and her family are from Somalia, and they had tried and failed to get their approved green cards from USCIS for three months. Luckily – and likely thanks to my office's intervention – they received their green cards promptly in the mail.

If you're having a problem with a federal agency, I'll do everything in my power to get it resolved – so please, don't hesitate to reach out!

There are plenty more wins and challenges in the months ahead, but together, I know we'll persevere. Thank you for being a part of this team.

There is work to be done,

Chrissy

name: Wes Moore Updates
subject: A recap of February wins
body:
Friend,

This February, our administration rolled up their sleeves and got straight to work!

We worked hard, Wes signed legislation, and we had some fun along the way. Here are some of the February highlights you may have missed:

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP30/1/90457/images/wm_heymaryland.png]

To start the month, we honored the 60th Anniversary of the Civil Rights Act and the start of Black History Month by exploring the stories of civil rights leaders like Thurgood Marshall, Juanita Jackson Mitchell, and Pauli Murray. We encourage folks to visit Maryland's Black history museums and landmarks all year long!

Earlier in February, Wes delivered the 2024 State of the State Address. He reflected on our successes over the last 12 months, and highlighted this year's plans to make Maryland safer, more affordable, more competitive, and the state that serves. If you missed it, you can watch the stream here. [https://twitter.com/GovWesMoore/status/1755271933288157659] But if there is one thing you should know, it’s that our state is strong.

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP30/1/90457/images/wm_legislating.jpeg]

Wes and Aruna also rolled out their top legislative priorities by supporting a package of 16 bills this session. As part of their agenda, Wes testified in support of the ENOUGH Act.

The ENOUGH Act is a data-backed approach to eliminate poverty across the state by strategically channeling state money and support toward our most impoverished neighborhoods. This legislation will help transform once-distressed communities into places with top-notch schools, good jobs, safe neighborhoods, affordable and quality housing, and economic momentum that uplifts businesses and entrepreneurs.

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP30/1/90457/images/wm_ravenshike.jpeg]Lastly — in celebration of the end of football season, Wes spent Lamar Jackson Day hiking Cross Island and Metapeake Trail on Kent Island. We might not have taken the Lombardi Trophy home this year, but watch out for next year!

A quick snapshot of February shows just how hard Wes is fighting for Marylanders. If you want to keep up with the latest, make sure to follow Wes on social media!

Follow on Facebook [https://www.facebook.com/iamwesmoore/]

Follow on Twitter (X) [https://twitter.com/iamwesmoore]

Follow on Instagram [https://instagram.com/iamwesmoore]

Thank you for your support,

Team Moore

name: The Office of Delegate Briana D. Sewell
subject: Del. Sewell's Week 8 Session Newsletter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Briana Sewell
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/New%20Sewell%20Delegate%20Logo%20.png]
Session Week 8 Newsletter
Dear Neighbor,
That’s it for the penultimate week of the 2024 regular General Assembly session! As we embark on the final week of the legislative session, my colleagues and I serving in the House of Delegates and state Senate must take final action on all bills considered by the body during this year’s convening.
Bills that are similar but not identical and pass both the House and Senate will go to a conference committee which consists of 3 members of each chamber to develop final compromise language. A majority of the conference committee members must agree on the final compromise language of the bill and send that final language in the form of a conference report to both bodies for a final vote. Both bodies have an opportunity to pass conference reports and send them to the other body for consideration.
If there are bills during this legislative session that you took a particular interest in or feel passionate about passing (or not passing) and you want to know the status, you can look them up individually on the Legislative Information System (LIS) here [https://lis.virginia.gov/] [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+men+BIL] [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+men+BIL] . You may search by bill number, or you may take a look at the entire docket of certain committees or all bills introduced by a single member by clicking one of the other sorting options.
Conference committee reports (these include the agreed-upon compromise language for bills that have been passed differently from the House and Senate) will be posted on LIS as they are agreed to, and as they pass or fail both legislative bodies.
Please stay in touch about your perspective on individual bills and conference reports or other issues that matter to you over the week and beyond. I always want to hear from you!
The end (of the budget process) is near
Just like other bills, the Virginia State Budget is a bill that must be passed uniformly by both the House and Senate. Each year, the individual House and Senate budgets are sent to conference and the budget conferees determine the final House and Senate compromise budget which goes to the governor’s desk.
On Sunday, February 18th, the House and Senate released their initial budget proposals which passed their respective chamber with overwhelming bipartisan support. This past week, the House and Senate conferees were announced. They are diligently working to finalize a joint budget to be approved by the General Assembly and eventually sent to Governor Glenn Youngkin for review.
The House conferees are:
Delegate Luke Torian (D)
Delegate Mark Sickles (D)
Delegate David Bulova (D)
Delegate Betsy Carr (D)
Delegate Terry Austin (R)
Delegate Robert Bloxom (R)
The Senate conferees are:
Senator L. Louise Lucas (D)
Senator Mamie Locke (D)
Senator Creigh Deeds (D)
Senator Jennifer Boysko (D)
Senator Todd Pillion (R)
Senator Ryan McDougle (R)
As we kick off the last week of the legislative session, the budget conferees are working hard and will soon release their compromise budget, which will then be sent to the Governor for consideration. All bills that passed both chambers of the General Assembly will also go to the Governor's desk. The General Assembly will reconvene in Richmond on Wednesday, April 16th to consider any changes the Governor makes to the budget and legislation before the body, including bills he chooses to veto.
While we do not know exactly what the final Senate and House compromise budget will contain at this moment, we do know that the House and Senate proposals made significant investments in the critical areas of education, healthcare, transportation, and mental health. The Democratic majority in the House and the Senate will stand firm in our commitment to protecting these common-sense investments that directly benefit Virginia's families.
Welcome to Richmond! Constituent Engagement and More
I appreciate everyone who visited me in Richmond this week to provide their input or feedback on legislation, update me on their organization, or just to say hello.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_5140.jpg] I had the opportunity to deliver remarks before the Democratic Business Council of Northern Virginia [https://dembiz.org/] (also known as DemBiz). I spoke about the importance of building a more inclusive, dynamic, and sustainable economy that can best serve the residents of Northern Virginia.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0691.JPG] My office joined Sen. Pillion’s office to take part in the Rapid REVIVE Training [https://dbhds.virginia.gov/behavioral-health/substance-abuse-services/revive/] , hosted by the Virginia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services (DBHDS) which provides life-saving training on how to recognize and effectively respond to an opioid overdose.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0630.jpg] My legislative assistant, Jay, welcomed students from James Madison University to my office to discuss how they can get involved in local government, their plans for post-graduation, and more. It’s always exciting to speak with the next generation of leaders!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0566.jpg] I’d like to thank VOICE [https://www.virginiavoice.org/] for stopping by to discuss their ongoing efforts to engage the faith communities in advocating for affordable housing, civic engagement, and mental health services. Thank you for everything you do!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0647.jpg] Team Sewell had a blast attending the “Breakfast with Robots” event and hearing from students involved in FIRST Robotics [https://www.firstinspires.org/robotics/frc] , a global youth empowerment nonprofit where students learn engineering and research skills by building their own robots and competing with other youth teams to complete tasks with those robots on a clock. The students were here in the General Assembly advocating for additional STEM+C funding so that Title I schools can provide these excellent extracurricular STEM opportunities to their students at no cost to the students participating.
Bills
My bills continue to move through the Senate. Check out their progress below: [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB738+]
HB731 works to fix the leaky teacher pipeline and increase teacher diversity through the elimination of a duplicative, expensive, and out-of-date testing requirement for teachers. The bill passed the full Senate Education and Health Committee unanimously, 15-0 and passed the full Senate on March 4th on a vote of 39-0.
HB732 requires schools to stock and train staff on the administration of Naloxone, a life-saving medication, in case of an opioid overdose. This bill passed the full Senate Education and Health Committee with a substitute unanimously, 15-0 and passed the full Senate on March 4th on a vote of 39-0 .
HB736 protects veterans from predatory Veterans Affairs benefits claim sharks. The Senate Commerce and Labor Committee passed the bill today. I look forward to working with Sen. Reeves, the VA Dept of Vet Services, the Veterans Service Organization's Joint Leadership Council, Veterans of Foreign Wars, and all other impacted community members to ensure our veterans hard earned benefits are protected against claim sharks. [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB738+]
This Week’s Mailbag
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-03-04%20at%204.32.27%20PM.png]
My team and I always appreciate your continued engagement about specific bills, budget items, and policies. We value your ongoing engagement and feedback!
This week, we received correspondence regarding the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) and environmental protections, bereavement leave, and skill games legislation.
If you have concerns or ideas about legislation before the House of Delegates, the upcoming budget, or anything else, you can always contact my office at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] .
Stay In Touch!
As we inch closer to the end of the 2024 General Assembly Session, remember to stay in touch! You may email my office at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] , call us at 703-261-4787, or visit my Richmond office in person at 201 North 9th Street, Suite 905, Richmond, Virginia 23219.
We look forward to hearing from you, and please stay tuned as we continue to provide important updates about legislation, the budget, the end of the session, and what our work looks like between now and the reconvene session in April.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/headingcommunitybill%20%281%29.png]

Louise Lucas (D) Senator Mamie Locke (D) Senator Creigh Deeds (D) Senator Jennifer Boysko (D) Senator Todd Pillion (R) Senator Ryan McDougle (R) As we kick off the last week of the legislative session, the budget conferees are working hard and will soon release their compromise budget, which will then be sent to the Governor for consideration. All bills that passed both chambers of the General Assembly will also go to the Governor's desk. The General Assembly will reconvene in Richmond on Wednesday, April 16th to consider any changes the Governor makes to the budget and legislation before the body, including bills he chooses to veto. While we do not know exactly what the final Senate and House compromise budget will contain at this moment, we do know that the House and Senate proposals made significant investments in the critical areas of education, healthcare, transportation, and mental health. The Democratic majority in the House and the Senate will stand firm in our commitment to protecting these common-sense investments that directly benefit Virginia's families. Welcome to Richmond! Constituent Engagement and More I appreciate everyone who visited me in Richmond this week to provide their input or feedback on legislation, update me on their organization, or just to say hello. [] I had the opportunity to deliver remarks before the Democratic Business Council of Northern Virginia [] (also known as DemBiz). I spoke about the importance of building a more inclusive, dynamic, and sustainable economy that can best serve the residents of Northern Virginia. [] My office joined Sen. Pillion’s office to take part in the Rapid REVIVE Training [] , hosted by the Virginia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services (DBHDS) which provides life-saving training on how to recognize and effectively respond to an opioid overdose. [] My legislative assistant, Jay, welcomed students from James Madison University to my office to discuss how they can get involved in local government, their plans for post-graduation, and more. It’s always exciting to speak with the next generation of leaders! [] I’d like to thank VOICE [] for stopping by to discuss their ongoing efforts to engage the faith communities in advocating for affordable housing, civic engagement, and mental health services. Thank you for everything you do! [] Team Sewell had a blast attending the “Breakfast with Robots” event and hearing from students involved in FIRST Robotics [] , a global youth empowerment nonprofit where students learn engineering and research skills by building their own robots and competing with other youth teams to complete tasks with those robots on a clock. The students were here in the General Assembly advocating for additional STEM+C funding so that Title I schools can provide these excellent extracurricular STEM opportunities to their students at no cost to the students participating. Bills My bills continue to move through the Senate. Check out their progress below: [+] HB731 works to fix the leaky teacher pipeline and increase teacher diversity through the elimination of a duplicative, expensive, and out-of-date testing requirement for teachers. The bill passed the full Senate Education and Health Committee unanimously, 15-0 and passed the full Senate on March 4th on a vote of 39-0. HB732 requires schools to stock and train staff on the administration of Naloxone, a life-saving medication, in case of an opioid overdose. This bill passed the full Senate Education and Health Committee with a substitute unanimously, 15-0 and passed the full Senate on March 4th on a vote of 39-0 . HB736 protects veterans from predatory Veterans Affairs benefits claim sharks. The Senate Commerce and Labor Committee passed the bill today. I look forward to working with Sen. Reeves, the VA Dept of Vet Services, the Veterans Service Organization's Joint Leadership Council, Veterans of Foreign Wars, and all other impacted community members to ensure our veterans hard earned benefits are protected against claim sharks. [+] This Week’s Mailbag [] My team and I always appreciate your continued engagement about specific bills, budget items, and policies. We value your ongoing engagement and feedback! This week, we received correspondence regarding the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) and environmental protections, bereavement leave, and skill games legislation. If you have concerns or ideas about legislation before the House of Delegates, the upcoming budget, or anything else, you can always contact my office at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] . Stay In Touch! As we inch closer to the end of the 2024 General Assembly Session, remember to stay in touch! You may email my office at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] , call us at 703-261-4787, or visit my Richmond office in person at 201 North 9th Street, Suite 905, Richmond, Virginia 23219. We look forward to hearing from you, and please stay tuned as we continue to provide important updates about legislation, the budget, the end of the session, and what our work looks like between now and the reconvene session in April. I serve God first

| |

Friend,

I'm the product of an unplanned pregnancy.

Born to two teenage parents, every statistic and societal roadblock indicated that I was destined for a life of hardship.

But my parents didn't buy into any of that.

I may have been unplanned, but that did not mean I was unwanted.

Soon after me, three more kids came. And what began as a teenage love story quickly became a family of six. My dad went to work and did whatever he needed to do to make ends meet for our family. That meant putting his life on the line to serve his community in the local fire department.

All my life, I wanted to be like my dad, and there was nothing I dreamed of more than becoming a firefighter just like him.

But on a fateful day in September of 1984, all of that changed.

My dad and his battalion responded to a call that would change all of our lives forever.

By the grace of God my dad made it out of that building alive, but not unscathed. Eighty percent of his body was covered in burns.

From then on, the hardest working man that I knew would not be able to work as a fireman another day of his life. And as the oldest of four kids, it was up to me to step in and help fill the void in our young family.

We're all a product of our experiences, and that moment defined who I am.

My dream of becoming a firefighter like my dad was now discouraged, and I had effectively been launched into the role of a pseudo-parent to my younger siblings overnight.

**Being raised in a Christian household without a lot of means, we put our head down for two reasons:

1\. To pray to God
2\. To get to work**

So, at 12 years old, I picked myself up by my bootstraps and did just that -- got to work.

And to be quite honest, I haven't really picked my head back up since.

>From a young boy trying to help his parents make ends meet, to a law student, to a husband and father, and eventually to Speaker of the House, the only thing I have ever been focused on is getting the job done.

My wife might call me a workaholic, but in my mind, I am a man who is focused on the task at hand, and completing a mission.

**[Right now, my mission is to ensure that my kids have the same opportunity to make a life for themselves and achieve their goals like I did.](http://links.fighttheswamp.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=343c048a5e4c42c5970b2db4d6d155c5&_e=6GrPcnoJjreB_KGPXLRBEQJ33wzgo8r-gDwQvqn7-ymBu6BL8xotmU-Kci1mhxXaFD2qrvFC7ukwrztyamuB5Uo5if3A15kqZph5NMgHezRCYX5KB2rdGSXlUqfG4XT9x5snletxrmbGmCOhVZLuLE3AxvpKqVVbt_Xmi8Gq01Zua0yICOxx4KBxWJGak_P6eEORlwUOtzXDUUBBAb-4o3TLJB_gdzUXZMGIKNchmqtP0z18I0ymL01bLuPCxH9In450PiBmmKtVTyvTzsJtbtP_G0wPqYjCR9-PUSE2Ixh5-xQIHFX_Ps-NWkr-RtwX9kqGu-YTK-2-eMxinvcGq5Cfu5gnPE4vlXkY2304Q106ZVE51sKdtzzPw_cZ6qFy7gzeEKnICFIXp_pTsjWHVVSJKSSinZlO3fqS3zfFbnGlVAu19XvPMou_8AMvzUsbmD2GKIm7wWmT8uNY4RUmwi0tDS5NqednacIX6G4N_LNBWhOlSWM9guOE0HqsPJkORCswaVulwJL_sf_7DEUiqQ%3D%3D "Right now, my mission is to ensure that my kids have the same opportunity to make a life for themselves and achieve their goals like I did. ")**

And that means being the kind of conservative, Christian leader in Washington, D.C. that my dad would be proud of.

That alone puts you at odds with the D.C. Establishment, by the way.

I'm not interested in the cocktail parties, or rubbing elbows with different special interest groups.

The Washington Elite and their allies in the mainstream media can cast judgment all they want. That doesn't bother me.

Because at the end of the day, I know that I serve an audience of one -- and that I am doing all that I can with the blessings given to me, and the faith entrusted to me, to glorify God.

**[So, now that you know just a little bit more about me, where I come from, and what keeps me going, I humbly ask if you are willing to stand alongside me in this fight?](http://links.fighttheswamp.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=343c048a5e4c42c5970b2db4d6d155c5&_e=6GrPcnoJjreB_KGPXLRBEQJ33wzgo8r-gDwQvqn7-ymBu6BL8xotmU-Kci1mhxXaFD2qrvFC7ukwrztyamuB5Uo5if3A15kqZph5NMgHezRCYX5KB2rdGSXlUqfG4XT9x5snletxrmbGmCOhVZLuLE3AxvpKqVVbt_Xmi8Gq01Zua0yICOxx4KBxWJGak_P6eEORlwUOtzXDUUBBAb-4o3TLJB_gdzUXZMGIKNchmqtP0z18I0ymL01bLuPCxH9In450PiBmmKtVTyvTzsJtbtP_G0wPqYjCR9-PUSE2Ixh5-xQIHFX_Ps-NWkr-RtwX9kqGu-YTK-2-eMxinvcGq5Cfu5gnPE4vlXkY2304Q106ZVE51sKdtzzPw_cZ6qFylvf-0Yoy32ndjtsxNvZnJVM8xBzdRrF6rCutJ_i3szPTA9N50lbQHl74SOZtKRvbggBnpfpx8w1hTNEtekn5oPiOnsDLtFzz8qPCHL30Rx0h-4hqsJglnp3pGXZmwSFsNlX_W9qmDfoAajcSnkxoiQ%3D%3D "So, now that you know just a little bit more about me, where I come from, and what keeps me going, I humbly ask if you are willing to stand alongside me in this fight? clean_body: I serve God first | | | | | | Friend, I'm the product of an unplanned pregnancy. Born to two teenage parents, every statistic and societal roadblock indicated that I was destined for a life of hardship. But my parents didn't buy into any of that. I may have been unplanned, but that did not mean I was unwanted. Soon after me, three more kids came. And what began as a teenage love story quickly became a family of six. My dad went to work and did whatever he needed to do to make ends meet for our family. That meant putting his life on the line to serve his community in the local fire department. All my life, I wanted to be like my dad, and there was nothing I dreamed of more than becoming a firefighter just like him. But on a fateful day in September of 1984, all of that changed. My dad and his battalion responded to a call that would change all of our lives forever. By the grace of God my dad made it out of that building alive, but not unscathed. Eighty percent of his body was covered in burns. From then on, the hardest working man that I knew would not be able to work as a fireman another day of his life. And as the oldest of four kids, it was up to me to step in and help fill the void in our young family. We're all a product of our experiences, and that moment defined who I am. My dream of becoming a firefighter like my dad was now discouraged, and I had effectively been launched into the role of a pseudo-parent to my younger siblings overnight. Being raised in a Christian household without a lot of means, we put our head down for two reasons: 1\. To pray to God 2\. To get to work So, at 12 years old, I picked myself up by my bootstraps and did just that -- got to work. And to be quite honest, I haven't really picked my head back up since. From a young boy trying to help his parents make ends meet, to a law student, to a husband and father, and eventually to Speaker of the House, the only thing I have ever been focused on is getting the job done. My wife might call me a workaholic, but in my mind, I am a man who is focused on the task at hand, and completing a mission. "Right now, my mission is to ensure that my kids have the same opportunity to make a life for themselves and achieve their goals like I did. " And that means being the kind of conservative, Christian leader in Washington, D.C. that my dad would be proud of. That alone puts you at odds with the D.C. Establishment, by the way. I'm not interested in the cocktail parties, or rubbing elbows with different special interest groups. The Washington Elite and their allies in the mainstream media can cast judgment all they want. That doesn't bother me. Because at the end of the day, I know that I serve an audience of one -- and that I am doing all that I can with the blessings given to me, and the faith entrusted to me, to glorify God. "So, now that you know just a little bit more about me, where I come from, and what keeps me going, I humbly ask if you are willing to stand alongside me in this fight? " | | I'm not going to lie to you, it won't be easy. But doing what's right rarely is. Thank you for your time and support, | Speaker Mike Johnson * | | | Paid for by Mike Johnson for Louisiana P.O. | | **A Note from CAPT Hung Cao USN (Ret)** It’s been a busy few days on the campaign trail! Last week I visited Virginia Beach, where former Congresswoman Thelma Drake welcomed us with a standing room only event. Later, I connected with the Hampton Roads Chamber of Commerce to discuss our community’s priorities, and I took a group of Martial Arts school owners and business leaders aboard the newest aircraft carrier in the Navy. Ending the week on a high note, I had the opportunity to meet with President Donald J. Trump at the annual Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) near Washington D.C. It was an honor to meet with him and discuss our plans to win Virginia this November, and take back our country. body:
Thierry literally ran to the fire | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/a72368ffa9a4/a-new-way-forward-for-texas-12683304?e=b8ba94fd9b)
---
When Texas was at one of its lowest points in modern history, Ted Cruz packed his bags and headed to Cancun.
Last week when the Panhandle was on fire during the worst wildfire in Texas history, Ted Cruz, Colin Allred, and everyone else running for the U.S. Senate didn’t show up. Thierry Tchenko dropped everything and drove 9 hours, overnight, to deliver aid and help the people who were struggling.
**Thierry is exactly the kind of person we need representing us in Washington, DC.**
[**Election Day is tomorrow. Kick in $20 or more today and let’s make sure this grassroots campaign has what it needs to finish strong.**](https://tchenkofortexas.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=93f02de4b9a588e8269491419&id=f9a20af6fe&e=b8ba94fd9b)
Thank you,Team TchenkoDemocratic Campaign for U.S. Senate

\---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: **Thierry Tchenko** <info@tchenkofortexas.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 29, 2024 at 2:21 PM
Subject: The Panhandle is on fire

My plan for this week was to host more campaign events and do everything I could to get out the vote.
But, on Tuesday night after an event in Galveston, I received news that wildfires had spread across 500,000 acres of land in the Panhandle.
I couldn’t sit idly while the Panhandle deals with one of the worst disasters in Texas’ history.
**So Gloria and I filled the car with water and supplies and drove 9 hours that night from Houston to provide support. We arrived Wednesday morning in Borger ready to serve.**
[](https://tchenkofortexas.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=93f02de4b9a588e8269491419&id=5b98367163&e=b8ba94fd9b)
**The people I’m meeting and the stories I’m hearing are surreal. And painful.**_**But we’re finding ways to be helpful so I’m glad we came.**_
If you want to help support the communities affected by the fire, the Lubbock-Avalanche Journal did a roundup of ways to do your part. [**Here’s the article**](https://tchenkofortexas.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=93f02de4b9a588e8269491419&id=1aaba3c703&e=b8ba94fd9b)**.**
If you’re in the area and we can be of any assistance, let us know. Our number is 713-364-5889. We’re here to help.
Thank you and God Bless,Thierry TchenkoDemocratic Candidate for U.S. Senate
PS - I’m sharing real-time updates and reactions on my TikTok channel. [**If you haven’t already, connect with me over there today.**](https://tchenkofortexas.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=93f02de4b9a588e8269491419&id=03c567623f&e=b8ba94fd9b)

That’s why the National Democratic Redistricting Committee has a 10 year plan to win fair maps, and they deserve our support. **The change we know is possible depends on working together to meet this moment and taking this challenge head on. For the last seven years, the NDRC has done the hard work of standing up to partisan and racial gerrymandering, and fighting for maps that lead to fair representation. Trust me, I know that work too often gets overshadowed by the louder parts of our politics. But it is essential to building a society in which everyone’s voice truly matters.
**Our democracy is stronger today because of your work with the NDRC. But our work is far from complete. **
Too many voters are still being silenced by gerrymandering. Too many people are being deliberately left out of our democracy thanks to rising attacks on voting rights. And unlike the days when congressional and legislative districts were redrawn once a decade, these fights are now happening every year in every corner of the country. In fact, several maps hang in the balance as I write this.
As Attorney General Holder likes to say, we’re now in an era of perpetual redistricting. For those of us who care deeply about this cause, that means we can’t take our foot off the gas, even for a moment.
The NDRC’s 10 Year Plan will not only protect the fair maps we’ve fought hard to achieve, it will also fight back against cynical, partisan efforts to further undermine our democracy.
**I’ve often said that change only happens when ordinary people get involved, get engaged, and come together to demand it._Now is the time to take a stand. _**

Thank you,
Barack Obama

clean_body: Will you join me in continuing to build the movement for fair maps? | Take a minute and think about where you want our country to be a decade from now. Personally, I want to do everything I can to create a fairer, more just, and more equal America. That starts by protecting our democracy from those who want to weaken it. This is a fight that won’t be won in one election or one court case — it requires a plan to fight back everywhere, every year. That’s why the National Democratic Redistricting Committee has a 10 year plan to win fair maps, and they deserve our support. The change we know is possible depends on working together to meet this moment and taking this challenge head on. So I’m asking: = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = For the last seven years, the NDRC has done the hard work of standing up to partisan and racial gerrymandering, and fighting for maps that lead to fair representation. Trust me, I know that work too often gets overshadowed by the louder parts of our politics. But it is essential to building a society in which everyone’s voice truly matters. Our democracy is stronger today because of your work with the NDRC. But our work is far from complete. Too many voters are still being silenced by gerrymandering. Too many people are being deliberately left out of our democracy thanks to rising attacks on voting rights. And unlike the days when congressional and legislative districts were redrawn once a decade, these fights are now happening every year in every corner of the country. In fact, several maps hang in the balance as I write this. As Attorney General Holder likes to say, we’re now in an era of perpetual redistricting. For those of us who care deeply about this cause, that means we can’t take our foot off the gas, even for a moment. The NDRC’s 10 Year Plan will not only protect the fair maps we’ve fought hard to achieve, it will also fight back against cynical, partisan efforts to further undermine our democracy. I’ve often said that change only happens when ordinary people get involved, get engaged, and come together to demand it.Now is the time to take a stand. = We’ve got a lot of work to do. And I’ll be right there with you as we do it. Thank you, Barack Obama = = Since 2017, the NDRC has executed a comprehensive redistricting strategy that shifts the redistricting power, creating fair districts where Democrats can compete. Our victories have been made possible by our strong community of grassroots supporters. = If you want to receive periodic updates from the NDRC on our fight for fair maps, text MAPS to 36787. Peter Willis, from our
immense sadness and disappointment with the U.S. government’s complicity
in the 30,000 deaths in Gaza and severe restrictions on humanitarian aid
that Palestinians need, we’re working hard to change President Biden’s
policies on Gaza.

When mass atrocities against Palestinians and widespread protests in
America weren’t enough to change Biden’s mind, we decided to move beyond
the moral case for Peace and cut to Biden’s fundamental self-interest.

That’s why we led a campaign in Michigan that brought out 100,000 folks to
make a Biden protest vote of Uncommitted. Now we’re launching an
Uncommitted campaign in Washington state and reaching out to our 132,000
members in the state.

message that his policies supporting Netanyahu’s war in Gaza must change.
Join 100,000 voters in Michigan and a groundswell of Uncommitted voters in
Washington state to say Ceasefire NOW.

clear. Both Biden and Vice President Harris have now mentioned a

progressive voters in the state via the media, social media, and our
growing megaphone for Peace. We need you right there with us, committed to
this Uncommitted protest vote alongside our organizers and voters in
states where Uncommitted is a voting option.

immediately.

When we organize, we win.

This week we got devastating news out of Alabama, where the state Supreme Court handed down a ruling effectively putting an end to in vitro fertilization, otherwise known as IVF, indefinitely.
Countless Americans rely each year on the IVF process to have a baby, but this ruling will mean that countless couples in Alabama will be left unable to bring a child into their lives.
When _Roe_ was overturned, I and many others warned that it was just the tip of the iceberg with how far Republicans nationwide would go to overturn Americans' rights to make health care decisions without government interference. Unfortunately, this latest news out of Alabama is further proof that we were right.
This ruling was the direct result of _Roe_ being overturned. But Republicans aren't going to stop at abortion – they're gleefully going after every facet of freedom in our personal lives. They won't rest until there's a politician in every exam room and bedroom in the country.
The decision to start a family is a deeply personal one, and one that brings joy to so many mothers and fathers around the country each and every day. Now, extremist Republicans have denied that right to start a family – denied that joy – to countless couples across Alabama.
Make no mistake: they won't stop here. Republican lawmakers have made it clear they've set their sights on everything from a national abortion ban, to contraception, the right to marry who you love, and many other deeply personal freedoms. If Republicans are allowed to regain control of the Senate and White House, and maintain control in the House this November, they will go after our fundamental rights. We can be certain of that.
Our country is at a crossroads, and our fundamental constitutional rights hang in the balance. It's never been more urgent that we reject Republican extremism in every corner of our nation and elect unapologetically pro-choice, progressive leaders to Congress. clean_body: | | | Just a few days ago, I wrote to you about the alarming situation in Alabama, where all in vitro fertilization (IVF) procedures have been thrown into doubt due to a recent court ruling handed down by Alabama's right-wing extremist Supreme Court. I'm reaching out again because last week, Senate Republicans blocked an effort by Democrats to pass legislation that would have protected IVF nationwide. In the wake of the Alabama ruling, my Republican colleagues spent days claiming to support access to IVF. Their actions say otherwise. Right-wing Republicans made this ruling possible when they gutted Roe v. Wade. And now, the party that claims to be the party of "family values" is denying an entire generation of women in Alabama the chance to become mothers through IVF. The right to start a family is a deeply personal decision that should be made between parents without government interference. But it's clear that Republican extremists won't rest until there's a politician in every bedroom and exam room in America. Republicans will stop at nothing to rip away Americans' fundamental rights and freedoms. We have to fight back, and that means expanding our Senate majority and retaking the House so there's no chance of Republicans jamming through their right-wing agenda. But I can't do it alone. = Onward, Ron Forwarded Message | This week we got devastating news out of Alabama, where the state Supreme Court handed down a ruling effectively putting an end to in vitro fertilization, otherwise known as IVF, indefinitely. Countless Americans rely each year on the IVF process to have a baby, but this ruling will mean that countless couples in Alabama will be left unable to bring a child into their lives. When Roe was overturned, I and many others warned that it was just the tip of the iceberg with how far Republicans nationwide would go to overturn Americans' rights to make health care decisions without government interference. Unfortunately, this latest news out of Alabama is further proof that we were right. This ruling was the direct result of Roe being overturned. But Republicans aren't going to stop at abortion – they're gleefully going after every facet of freedom in our personal lives. They won't rest until there's a politician in every exam room and bedroom in the country. The decision to start a family is a deeply personal one, and one that brings joy to so many mothers and fathers around the country each and every day. Now, extremist Republicans have denied that right to start a family – denied that joy – to countless couples across Alabama. Make no mistake: they won't stop here. Republican lawmakers have made it clear they've set their sights on everything from a national abortion ban, to contraception, the right to marry who you love, and many other deeply personal freedoms. If Republicans are allowed to regain control of the Senate and White House, and maintain control in the House this November, they will go after our fundamental rights. We can be certain of that. Our country is at a crossroads, and our fundamental constitutional rights hang in the balance. It's never been more urgent that we reject Republican extremism in every corner of our nation and elect unapologetically pro-choice, progressive leaders to Congress. = I'm all in on this fight, and I hope you're with me. That's because the anti-Trump Media... Young radicals on college campuses... the holier-than-thou elites in Hollywood... Democrat Super PACs... Joe Biden's army of megadonors... They are fully committed to destroying our movement and replacing EVERY LAST ONE OF US with a Liberal Democrat.

But wait, that's not even the half of it. It gets worse:
** Problem #1: ** We have TWO imminent Special Elections and Democrats committed more than five million dollars to install more Liberals.

** Problem #2: ** House Democrats have forty million bucks stashed away to attack pro-Trump Conservatives like us.

** Problem #3: ** Joe Biden just bragged about raising a million bucks in a SINGLE DAY attacking President Trump.
I cannot stress the urgency of the situation enough. Early voting is about to start in the first Special Election AND the Left's fundraising advantage grows by the minute...

If we fail to hit it, the consequences would be unthinkable. We'd have no choice but to: **1) ** SCRAP our get-out-the-vote operations, **2) ** SLASH the budget for our ad campaigns, and **3) ** Throw our digital outreach plans IN THE TRASH CAN.

Dear Peter,
Like my friend RFK, Jr., I too was a lifelong Democrat. But the party of hardworking American families has largely abandoned them, and is now the party of tech billionaires.
Unfortunately, they are also now the party of censorship, divisiveness, and forever wars.
Neither establishment party has plans to help the American middle class. This middle class has been the backbone and strength of our country. It is what made America the most prosperous nation on earth and the envy of the world.
Through Robert Kennedy, we have a man who will fight for the soul of our Nation. A man of integrity and heart who wishes nothing more than to restore the hope for every American that their hard work will once again allow them and their children to live a better life.
And to ensure that the lifeblood of America, freedom, and individual liberty not only continues, but flourishes!
**But Robert needs our help now more than ever.**
[DONATE NOW](https://www.kennedy24.com/donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=rob_schneider_3_4_24_nd3&n=5)
After surviving the negative attack ads and character assaults, the mainstream media has gone into its next phase of holding up the rickety establishment facade, ignoring Mr. Kennedy and excluding him from the public debate.
With your help, together we can make the establishment political machine and their paid cronies in the media talk about the issues that Americans actually care about most: the stability of our economy and our country; the health of our children and ourselves; ending taxpayer-funded forever wars; and putting up firewalls between industry and government agencies.
Together we can.
Together we must.
Together we WILL.
Together with Kennedy!

clean_body: The Connect the Grid Act would fix Texas’s broken power grid Big news, Peter: The San Antonio Express-News editorial board just endorsed my Connect the Grid Act! There’s lots of momentum behind my bill to fix Texas’s broken power grid—and I want to tell you more about it in a second. = = **= Peter, two weeks ago I introduced a new bill to connect Texas’s power grid to the nation’s supply, called the Connect the Grid Act. This bill would help prevent mass blackouts like those during Winter Storm Uri, and it would create more sustainable energy across America. For too long, politicians like Greg Abbott have kept our state’s power grid broken while collecting millions from billionaire donors who benefit from the status quo. They’ve kept our grid isolated from the nation’s power supply, and left Texans vulnerable to disasters. But as the San Antonio Express-News points out, my bill offers a way forward to a more reliable and sustainable power grid in Texas. = With a strong push from folks like you, we can rally support for this bill and fix Texas’s broken grid. = Thank you for supporting this work, -Greg Greg Casar Congressman Texas Congressional District 35 P.S.
